to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
tools.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tabId.description: Tab ID to execute the action on. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

save_to_disk.description: For screenshot/zoom actions: save the image to disk so it can be attached to a message for the user. Returns the saved path in the tool result. Only set this when you intend to share the image — screenshots you're just looking at don't need saving.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__find
tools.description: Find elements on the page using natural language. Can search for elements by their purpose (e.g., "search bar", "login button") or by text content (e.g., "organic mango product"). Returns up to 20 matching elements with references that can be used with other tools. If more than 20 matches exist, you'll be notified to use a more specific query. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find (e.g., "search bar", "add to cart button", "product title containing organic")

tabId.description: Tab ID to search in. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__get_page_text
tools.description: Extract raw text content from the page, prioritizing article content. Ideal for reading articles, blog posts, or other text-heavy pages. Returns plain text without HTML formatting. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

tabId.description: Tab ID to extract text from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a URL, or go forward/back in browser history. tabId may be omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate STANDALONE (not inside browser_batch): tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you and the first tab in the session's group is navigated — its result is appended to this call's output so you have the tab list and ids for subsequent calls. Inside browser_batch, navigate (and other tools that act on a page) requires an explicit tabId. Pass an explicit tabId when you need a specific tab or when the session's group has multiple tabs whose state you must preserve. tabId is required for url:"back"/"forward". A tab opened for you this way is yours to clean up, the same as one from tabs_create_mcp: close it with tabs_close_mcp once you no longer need it and before finishing your task, unless the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

url.description: The URL to navigate to. Can be provided with or without protocol (defaults to https://). Use "forward" to go forward in history or "back" to go back in history.

tabId.description: Tab ID to navigate. Must be a tab in the current group. If omitted for URL navigation when calling navigate standalone, tabs_context_mcp{createIfEmpty:true} is called for you. Required for url:"back"/"forward" and for navigate (and other tools that act on a page) inside browser_batch.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages
tools.description: Read browser console messages (console.log, console.error, console.warn, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging JavaScript errors, viewing application logs, or understanding what's happening in the browser console. Returns console messages from the current domain only. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs. IMPORTANT: Always provide a pattern to filter messages - without a pattern, you may get too many irrelevant messages.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read console messages from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

onlyErrors.description: If true, only return error and exception messages. Default is false (return all message types).

clear.description: If true, clear the console messages after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to filter console messages. Only messages matching this pattern will be returned (e.g., 'error|warning' to find errors and warnings, 'MyApp' to filter app-specific logs). You should always provide a pattern to avoid getting too many irrelevant messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
tools.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

# Findings — what we learned the hard way

**Tasks are not here any more.** Work is claimed in GitHub Issues:

```bash
gh issue list                  # what's open
gh issue list --assignee ""    # what's free
gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me
```

This file is for the other thing: numbers that turned out wrong, two people
colliding, traps that cost someone an hour. Things you need *before* you
pitch or before you merge, which don't belong in a task.

Add to it when you find one. It's cheaper than the next person finding it
again.

Last updated: **2026-11-08**

---

## Discovery steps 1–2 are live (2026-11-08, Jeremy, `frontend/live-agent`)

Patient analysis + profile agents now stream from Neo's `backend/agent` over
SSE (`frontend/src/lib/agent-api.ts`) instead of the timer. If `:8001` isn't
up when you press Run, it falls back to the scripted run; the header badge
says **Live agent** or **Simulated**. The page moves from analysis to profiles
by itself when the orchestrator fans out. DRKG + research steps are still
scripted.

- **Neo — one line in your file:** `graph.py`'s `plan` event now also carries
  `rationale`, so the UI can show the orchestrator's reasoning. Additive only.
- The agent reads `backend/data/patient/alex.json`, **not** the PDF uploaded in
  the browser (`VITE_AGENT_PATIENT` to change). Sending the PDF to
  `POST /api/patients` is the obvious next step; it adds ~45 s of Opus.
- "Five agents" is `AGENT_MAX_SUBAGENTS=5` in your local `backend/agent/.env`;
  the planner may still pick 3–5. Lanes render from the plan, so any count works.
- Rehearse with `VITE_AGENT_REPLAY_RUN=<run_id>`: replays a recorded run at
  real speed, no API spend.

## Repo reorg (2026-11-08): only `frontend/` and `backend/` at the top

`agent/`, `contract/`, `data/` → `backend/`; the six diagnostic dirs →
`backend/diagnostics/`. If your branch predates this, merge `main` in —
git follows the renames — but **new files you added at the old paths will
land at the old paths**; `git mv` them under `backend/`. Agent commands now
run from `backend/`; contract is `npm test --prefix backend/contract`.

## ⚠ Two people are building the same pipeline right now

**Jeremy** has the five-stage discovery pipeline in `frontend/` — scripted
TypeScript, `MATCHES` hand-written, labelled "Simulated".

**Levi** has `backend/query-generation/` on `agentic-query-generation` —
**five real Python agents** (`disease-indications`, `genes-targets`,
`pathways-processes`, `safety-interactions-class`, `symptoms-function`)
plus `ranking/intersection.py` and `ranking/fallback.py`, grounded in DRKG
and gated on human ALS exposure.

That is the same five agents, twice. One is the demo, one is the engine,
and **they share no git history** — `agentic-query-generation` has no merge
base with `main`.

Whoever picks this up: the cheapest win in the repo is making Jeremy's
`PipelineEvent` stream come from Levi's agents instead of a timer. The seam
already exists. Talk before either of you builds further.

**Neo** has a third piece, `backend/agent/` (PR #4): a Claude orchestrator that plans
ALS criteria and runs parallel LLM sub-agents that return drug-free *target
profiles* (genes + desired action, pathways, site). These are the anchors
Levi's DRKG agents need, and its SSE stream is a live source for Jeremy's
`PipelineEvent`s. How to combine all three without building a fourth:
[`RESEARCH_AGENT_HANDOFF.md`](RESEARCH_AGENT_HANDOFF.md).

## Found while auditing — read before you pitch

Measured against Neo's real `pipeline.json` on `cursor/pipeline-graph-ui`,
not the sample. Full citations in [`FUS_RESEARCH.md`](FUS_RESEARCH.md).

1. **The graveyard overstates `never_arrived`.** 24 `never_arrived` / 8
   `arrived_failed` — but **21 of the 24 have no BBB prediction at all**
   (biologics, or out of the model's domain). `src/merge.py:211-214` files
   "no prediction" as `never_arrived`. Only ceftriaxone (p 0.39),
   pentoxifylline (0.29) and pioglitazone (0.29) are actually predicted
   BBB-negative. Honest split: **3 / 8 / 21 undetermined.** Say "3 predicted
   never-arrived, 21 we can't call" on stage, never "24" — a judge who knows
   gabapentin crosses the BBB will catch it.
2. **Same error in the funnel.** "2,440 eliminated: predicted BBB-negative"
   is **1,593 predicted negative + 847 out of domain.** The honest number is
   still the strong one: **1,593 approved drugs the model says can't cross.**
   That is the FUS-unlocked pool — use it.
3. **Discovery stage 3 is fake while a real one exists.** `MATCHES` in
   `frontend/src/lib/pipeline.ts` is hand-written; Neo's `src/drkg.py` loads
   the real DRKG TransE vectors. Note DRKG embeds *entities*, not text, so a
   profile has to become DRKG genes before it has a vector — Jeremy's
   profiles already list target genes, so that bridge is short.
4. **Three knowledge graphs and two FaceChecks exist.** Graph: Neo's
   `GraphCanvas`, Henri's stale `KnowledgeGraph.tsx`, and a "coming soon"
   placeholder on `main`. FaceCheck: Neo's TS original and Levi's JS port.
   Pick one of each.

## If main gives you a `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` conflict — read this first

**Jeremy, this is the one you're hitting.** `frontend/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`
is TypeScript's incremental build cache. It was committed by mistake, it
rewrites itself on every single build, so it conflicted constantly. `main`
untracked it on 2026-11-07 and it's gitignored now.

Your branch has it modified, main deleted it → modify/delete conflict.
Accept the deletion; it regenerates on your next build and will never come
back:

```bash
git rm --cached frontend/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo
git commit --no-edit
```

One time only. Sorry — that one's on Henri, and it was the only file under
`frontend/` that main touched.

## Heads-up if you merge main

`main` deleted `app/` on 2026-11-07, so branches that built there get
modify/delete conflicts (measured: 11 on `cursor/pipeline-graph-ui`, 19 on
`frontend/kg-and-provenance`).

The standalone diagnostic suite was integrated from `codex/diagnostic-tests` by joining its original history to main. The additional FaceCheck integration remains on `Master-UI-Neo-Face-Integration`. See issue #18 and the root README for the merge and launcher.

The first step now runs on the real agent. The backend is usable, with three gaps I fixed or worked around on the way in. One real run worked end to end. **I haven't seen it in the browser yet**: the Chrome extension isn't connected, so the UI side is checked by the TypeScript compiler only.

**Is the backend ready?**
- **The streaming API was ready.** It sends every event as it happens, accepts requests from localhost and records each run.
- **The first agent makes no tool calls.** Its planning is one Opus call taking about 23 s, and it didn't send its reasoning to the UI. I added the reasoning to its `plan` event; that's one line in Neo's `graph.py`, logged for him in `docs/STATUS.md`.
- **It wasn't fixed at 5 agents.** It picks 3 up to a cap, and your local `backend/agent/.env` had the cap at 8. I set it to 5 there (only your machine). The UI builds its columns from the plan, so any number works.

**What the frontend does now**
- **Analysis page:** the orchestrator's trace shows loading the record, then "planning", then its written plan, then one `spawn_subagent` entry per brief.
- **Profiles page:** the app moves here by itself the moment the plan arrives. Each agent column shows its brief and its tool calls (PubMed, trials, Open Targets) as they happen, then its 1–3 profiles and the final ranking.
- **Fallback:** if the backend isn't running when you press Run, you get the old scripted run. A badge in the header says **Live agent** or **Simulated**.
- **Steps 3–4** (drug matching and the report) are still scripted.

**The test run:** 96 s, 5 agents, 12 profiles, nothing dropped by evidence checking. It's saved as `r20261108-021643-3a9717`, so you can rehearse with no API cost by setting `VITE_AGENT_REPLAY_RUN` to that id.

**To watch it:** I left two servers running.
- The agent API on :8001.
- A second copy of the frontend on :5174. It replays that recorded run, with sign-in switched off. Open `http://localhost:5174/home/case`, add the PDF and press Run.

Your own dev server on :5173 already has the changes. A run there goes to the live agent and costs money.

**Problems the run showed, in Neo's code (logged, not fixed):**
- The drug-name filter replaced "TDP-43" with "[drug]" in the summary, so it's removing biology terms.
- The backend's patient file says **Alex Moreau**, but the frontend case says **Alex Chen**.
- The agent always reads the backend's `alex` record, not the PDF you upload. Sending the PDF to the backend is the next step; expect it to add about 45 s.

Another Claude session reviewed the code and found two real bugs: a dropped connection could silently skip an agent's results, and a dead backend left the run stuck with no way out. Both are fixed, and I replied to it.

**Housekeeping:**

# Findings — what we learned the hard way

**Tasks are not here any more.** Work is claimed in GitHub Issues:

```bash
gh issue list                  # what's open
gh issue list --assignee ""    # what's free
gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me
```

This file is for the other thing: numbers that turned out wrong, two people
colliding, traps that cost someone an hour. Things you need *before* you
pitch or before you merge, which don't belong in a task.

Add to it when you find one. It's cheaper than the next person finding it
again.

Last updated: **2026-11-08**

---

## Discovery steps 1–2 are live (2026-11-08, Jeremy, `frontend/live-agent`)

Patient analysis + profile agents now stream from Neo's `backend/agent` over
SSE (`frontend/src/lib/agent-api.ts`) instead of the timer. If `:8001` isn't
up when you press Run, it falls back to the scripted run; the header badge
says **Live agent** or **Simulated**. The page moves from analysis to profiles
by itself when the orchestrator fans out. DRKG + research steps are still
scripted.

- **Neo — one line in your file:** `graph.py`'s `plan` event now also carries
  `rationale`, so the UI can show the orchestrator's reasoning. Additive only.
- The agent reads `backend/data/patient/alex.json`, **not** the PDF uploaded in
  the browser (`VITE_AGENT_PATIENT` to change). Sending the PDF to
  `POST /api/patients` is the obvious next step; it adds ~45 s of Opus.
- "Five agents" is `AGENT_MAX_SUBAGENTS=5` in your local `backend/agent/.env`;
  the planner may still pick 3–5. Lanes render from the plan, so any count works.
- Rehearse with `VITE_AGENT_REPLAY_RUN=<run_id>`: replays a recorded run at
  real speed, no API spend. A verified one for Alex: `r20261108-021643-3a9717`
  (96 s, 5 agents, 12 profiles). It lives in `backend/agent/runs/` (gitignored).
- **Neo — two bugs that run surfaced (not fixed):** `no_drugs.py` scrubs
  **"TDP-43" → "[drug]"** in the synthesis summary ("involves [drug]
  proteinopathy"; 20 removals that run), so it's over-matching biology terms.
  And `backend/data/patient/alex.json` says **Alex Moreau**, while the
  frontend case (`alex-case.ts`) says **Alex Chen**. A judge will see both names.

## Repo reorg (2026-11-08): only `frontend/` and `backend/` at the top

`agent/`, `contract/`, `data/` → `backend/`; the six diagnostic dirs →
`backend/diagnostics/`. If your branch predates this, merge `main` in —
git follows the renames — but **new files you added at the old paths will
land at the old paths**; `git mv` them under `backend/`. Agent commands now
run from `backend/`; contract is `npm test --prefix backend/contract`.

## ⚠ Two people are building the same pipeline right now

**Jeremy** has the five-stage discovery pipeline in `frontend/` — scripted
TypeScript, `MATCHES` hand-written, labelled "Simulated".

**Levi** has `backend/query-generation/` on `agentic-query-generation` —
**five real Python agents** (`disease-indications`, `genes-targets`,
`pathways-processes`, `safety-interactions-class`, `symptoms-function`)
plus `ranking/intersection.py` and `ranking/fallback.py`, grounded in DRKG
and gated on human ALS exposure.

That is the same five agents, twice. One is the demo, one is the engine,
and **they share no git history** — `agentic-query-generation` has no merge
base with `main`.

Whoever picks this up: the cheapest win in the repo is making Jeremy's
`PipelineEvent` stream come from Levi's agents instead of a timer. The seam
already exists. Talk before either of you builds further.

**Neo** has a third piece, `backend/agent/` (PR #4): a Claude orchestrator that plans
ALS criteria and runs parallel LLM sub-agents that return drug-free *target
profiles* (genes + desired action, pathways, site). These are the anchors
Levi's DRKG agents need, and its SSE stream is a live source for Jeremy's
`PipelineEvent`s. How to combine all three without building a fourth:
[`RESEARCH_AGENT_HANDOFF.md`](RESEARCH_AGENT_HANDOFF.md).

## Found while auditing — read before you pitch

Measured against Neo's real `pipeline.json` on `cursor/pipeline-graph-ui`,
not the sample. Full citations in [`FUS_RESEARCH.md`](FUS_RESEARCH.md).

1. **The graveyard overstates `never_arrived`.** 24 `never_arrived` / 8
   `arrived_failed` — but **21 of the 24 have no BBB prediction at all**
   (biologics, or out of the model's domain). `src/merge.py:211-214` files
   "no prediction" as `never_arrived`. Only ceftriaxone (p 0.39),
   pentoxifylline (0.29) and pioglitazone (0.29) are actually predicted
   BBB-negative. Honest split: **3 / 8 / 21 undetermined.** Say "3 predicted
   never-arrived, 21 we can't call" on stage, never "24" — a judge who knows
   gabapentin crosses the BBB will catch it.
2. **Same error in the funnel.** "2,440 eliminated: predicted BBB-negative"
   is **1,593 predicted negative + 847 out of domain.** The honest number is
   still the strong one: **1,593 approved drugs the model says can't cross.**
   That is the FUS-unlocked pool — use it.
3. **Discovery stage 3 is fake while a real one exists.** `MATCHES` in
   `frontend/src/lib/pipeline.ts` is hand-written; Neo's `src/drkg.py` loads
   the real DRKG TransE vectors. Note DRKG embeds *entities*, not text, so a
   profile has to become DRKG genes before it has a vector — Jeremy's
   profiles already list target genes, so that bridge is short.
4. **Three knowledge graphs and two FaceChecks exist.** Graph: Neo's
   `GraphCanvas`, Henri's stale `KnowledgeGraph.tsx`, and a "coming soon"
   placeholder on `main`. FaceCheck: Neo's TS original and Levi's JS port.
   Pick one of each.

## If main gives you a `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` conflict — read this first

**Jeremy, this is the one you're hitting.** `frontend/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`
is TypeScript's incremental build cache. It was committed by mistake, it
rewrites itself on every single build, so it conflicted constantly. `main`
untracked it on 2026-11-07 and it's gitignored now.

Your branch has it modified, main deleted it → modify/delete conflict.
Accept the deletion; it regenerates on your next build and will never come
back:

```bash
git rm --cached frontend/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo
git commit --no-edit
```

One time only. Sorry — that one's on Henri, and it was the only file under
`frontend/` that main touched.

## Heads-up if you merge main

`main` deleted `app/` on 2026-11-07, so branches that built there get
modify/delete conflicts (measured: 11 on `cursor/pipeline-graph-ui`, 19 on
`frontend/kg-and-provenance`).

The standalone diagnostic suite was integrated from `codex/diagnostic-tests` by joining its original history to main. The additional FaceCheck integration remains on `Master-UI-Neo-Face-Integration`. See issue #18 and the root README for the merge and launcher.

message.content: Exactly how does the backend integration work? I thought FastAPI was being used for the frontend to call the backend AI endpoints and communicate with its tool calls and responses?

content.text:
Yes, it's FastAPI. Your picture is right except for one thing: **the frontend only watches.** It doesn't take part in the tool calls or answer them. Every LLM call and every tool call runs inside the Python process. FastAPI just lets the browser start a run and then streams back a log of what's happening.

```
Browser (frontend/)                         FastAPI (backend/agent/api.py, :8001)
───────────────────                         ─────────────────────────────────────
1. POST /api/research ───────────────────►  creates a Run, starts the LangGraph graph
   {question, patient_id: "alex"}           as a background task, returns at once
   ◄──────────────── {run_id, events_url}

2. GET /api/research/{run_id}/events ────►  Server-Sent Events: one long-lived HTTP
   (EventSource; one-way, server → browser)  response, one event pushed per step
   ◄── run_started
   ◄── patient_loaded                        graph.py   load_patient
   ◄── plan  {rationale, briefs[5]}          graph.py   plan: one Opus call
   ◄── subagent_started  ×5                  graph.py   fan_out → 5 parallel research nodes
   ◄── tool_call {tool, args}                subagent.py  Sonnet agent decides to call a tool
   ◄── tool_result {tool, chars, error}      mcp_server.py runs it (PubMed, trials, Open Targets)
   ◄── subagent_finished {goals, targets}
   ◄── verify / report / run_finished        graph.py   verify → synthesize
```

**Inside the backend:**
1. **Starting a run.** `POST /api/research` creates a `Run` object and fires `execute()` as an asyncio task. It returns the `run_id` straight away instead of waiting the ~100 s for the run to finish.
2. **Events.** `execute()` runs the LangGraph graph in streaming mode. Each node announces its progress through LangGraph's stream writer (`_emit(...)` in `graph.py`). The sub-agents do the same: `subagent.py`'s `_handle()` turns each tool call Claude makes into a `tool_call` event, and each tool response into a `tool_result` event.
3. **Tools.** The sub-agents are LangChain agents running Claude Sonnet. Their tools come from `mcp_server.py`, an MCP server started as a separate subprocess. Claude picks a tool, LangChain calls it over MCP, and the result goes back to Claude. The frontend never sees that loop, only the events describing it.
4. **Fan-out.** Every event goes through `Run.push()`. That appends it to an in-memory list, writes it to `backend/agent/runs/<run_id>.jsonl` (the recording), and wakes the open SSE connection, which sends it to the browser.
5. **Replay.** If the `run_id` isn't in memory, the same `/events` endpoint reads the `.jsonl` file and sends its events again at the original timing. That's the free replay.

**On the frontend:**
- `frontend/src/lib/agent-api.ts` makes the POST, opens the stream, and translates each backend event into the `PipelineEvent` shape the scripted demo already used. For example, `tool_call` becomes a trace row in that agent's column.
- From there the existing `run-store.tsx` and the pages render it exactly as they rendered the script. That's why the UI code barely changed.

**What doesn't come through today.** The trace shows *that* each step happened, not everything in it:
- **Tool results arrive as a size only**, e.g. "2,728 characters returned", not the PubMed text.
- **There's no streaming text.** The orchestrator's plan shows up whole after ~23 s, and the sub-agents' reasoning between tool calls isn't sent at all.
- **It's one-way.** The browser can start a run and watch it, but it can't steer it, answer an agent, or cancel it. Pressing "Clear run" only stops the watching; the backend run carries on.

Any of these is a small change in the backend: put the real content into the event that's already being sent. The SSE plumbing already exists. The cheapest win is putting a short snippet of each tool result into `tool_result`, so the trace shows what PubMed actually returned.

+
+**What:** k-means (k = 24) on PCA-50 of the 400-d vectors; islands placed by

+size = log degree, shape = entity type. Supersedes the PCA-3 entry below.

+illustrative; every number on screen is still true 400-d L2.
+
+## 2026-11-08 — Stage 3 matches with the TransE query, not average + cosine
+
+**What:** Each profile target gene resolves to `Gene::<Entrez>` and gives a
+query `q = e[gene] − r[DRUGBANK::target::Compound:Gene]`. Every
+`Compound::DB#####` is scored by 400-d L2 to `q`, a profile keeps each
+compound's smallest distance over its genes, top 5 per profile. Precomputed
+by `frontend/scripts/drkg_scene.py` into `frontend/public/drkg/`.
+**Why:** TransE is fit so head + relation ≈ tail under L2, so `e[gene] − r` is
+where a drug targeting that gene should sit. Averaging unrelated genes lands
+*between* hypotheses; Levi's agents use the same min-over-anchors rule.
+**Rules out:** the "average + cosine" wording in `DISCOVERY_SPEC.md` §2 and
+#9, and embedding profile prose as text.
+
+## 2026-11-08 — The stage-3 picture is one linear PCA of all of DRKG
+
+**What:** All 97,238 entity vectors go through one global PCA to 3D, and query
+points use the same projection. On-screen numbers are true 400-d L2.
+**Why:** A linear map preserves vector addition, so the `gene − r → query`
+arrow on screen *is* the arithmetic, not an illustration of it. UMAP/t-SNE
+would cluster prettier but break that (and UMAP needs numba, no 3.14 wheels).
+**Rules out:** reading closeness off the 3D picture. Projected distance is not
+the ranking; the scene captions this.

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'

/**
 * Loads the precomputed DRKG scene written by `frontend/scripts/drkg_scene.py`
 * into `public/drkg/`. Nothing here computes embeddings: positions are a PCA-3
 * projection of the 400-d TransE vectors, distances are the true 400-d L2.
 */

export type Vec3 = [number, number, number]

export type DrkgGene = {
  symbol: string
  id: string
  row: number
  pos: Vec3
  /** Projection of e[gene] − r[target]. PCA is linear, so the arrow pos → query is exact. */
  query: Vec3
  targetEdges: number
  alsEdge: string | null
}

export type DrkgMatch = {
  rank: number
  id: string
  row: number
  name: string
  pos: Vec3
  /** True 400-d L2 from the profile's query. */
  distance: number
  viaGene: string
  directEdge: boolean
}

export type DrkgProfile = {
  lane: number
  name: string
  genes: DrkgGene[]
  unresolved: string[]
  matches: DrkgMatch[]
  edges: { from: number; to: number; rel: string }[]
}

export type DrkgScene = {
  meta: {
    model: string
    entities: number
    projection: string
    /** null for the clustered (non-linear) layout */
    explainedVariance: number[] | null
    relation: string
    formula: string
    universe: number
    topK: number
    /** Graph degree summary; present once `degree.bin` is written. */
    degree?: { min: number; median: number; p99: number; max: number }
  }
  types: { name: string; count: number }[]
  /** Optional: written once the layout is clustered; `clusters.bin` indexes into it. */
  clusters?: { id: number; label: string; size: number; dominantType: string; color?: string }[]
  als: { id: string; row: number; pos: Vec3; label: string }
  profiles: DrkgProfile[]
  handWritten: { drug: string; lane: number; source: string; id: string | null; rank: number | null; distance: number | null }[]
}

export type DrkgData = { scene: DrkgScene; positions: Float32Array; types: Uint8Array; clusters: Uint8Array | null; degree: Uint32Array | null }

/** A run is a folder: `scene.json` plus the binaries written beside it. Point `src` at a live backend's run. */
export const DEFAULT_SRC = '/drkg/scene.json'

const dirOf = (src: string) => src.slice(0, src.lastIndexOf('/') + 1)

async function get(url: string) {
  const res = await fetch(url)
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${url}: ${res.status}`)
  return res
}

const runs = new Map<string, Promise<DrkgData>>()
const nameCache = new Map<string, Promise<Record<string, string>>>()

export function loadDrkg(src = DEFAULT_SRC) {
  let run = runs.get(src)
  if (run) return run
  const base = dirOf(src)
  run = Promise.all([
    get(src).then((r) => r.json() as Promise<DrkgScene>),
    get(base + 'points.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer()),
    get(base + 'types.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer()),
    get(base + 'clusters.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer(), () => null),
    get(base + 'degree.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer(), () => null),
  ]).then(([scene, p, t, c, d]) => ({
    scene,
    positions: new Float32Array(p),
    types: new Uint8Array(t),
    // Vite's dev server answers a missing file with index.html, so check the length too.
    clusters: c && c.byteLength === t.byteLength && scene.clusters ? new Uint8Array(c) : null,
    degree: d && d.byteLength === t.byteLength * 4 && scene.meta.degree ? new Uint32Array(d) : null,
  }))
  runs.set(src, run)
  run.catch(() => runs.delete(src)) // let a later mount retry
  return run
}

/** Hover labels for every entity; ~1 MB, so only fetched on first hover. */
export function loadNames(src = DEFAULT_SRC) {
  let names = nameCache.get(src)
  if (!names) {
    names = get(dirOf(src) + 'names.json').then((r) => r.json())
    nameCache.set(src, names)
    names.catch(() => nameCache.delete(src))
  }
  return names
}

export function useDrkg(src = DEFAULT_SRC) {
  const [state, setState] = useState<{ data: DrkgData | null; error: string | null }>({ data: null, error: null })
  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true
    loadDrkg(src).then(
      (data) => live && setState({ data, error: null }),
      (e: Error) => live && setState({ data: null, error: e.message }),
    )
    return () => {
      live = false
    }
  }, [src])
  return state
}

import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'

/**
 * Loads the precomputed DRKG scene written by `frontend/scripts/drkg_scene.py`
 * into `public/drkg/`. Nothing here computes embeddings: positions are a PCA-3
 * projection of the 400-d TransE vectors, distances are the true 400-d L2.
 */

export type Vec3 = [number, number, number]

export type DrkgGene = {
  symbol: string
  id: string
  row: number
  pos: Vec3
  /** Projection of e[gene] − r[target]. PCA is linear, so the arrow pos → query is exact. */
  query: Vec3
  targetEdges: number
  alsEdge: string | null
}

export type DrkgMatch = {
  rank: number
  id: string
  row: number
  name: string
  pos: Vec3
  /** True 400-d L2 from the profile's query. */
  distance: number
  viaGene: string
  directEdge: boolean
}

export type DrkgProfile = {
  lane: number
  name: string
  genes: DrkgGene[]
  unresolved: string[]
  matches: DrkgMatch[]
  edges: { from: number; to: number; rel: string }[]
}

export type DrkgScene = {
  meta: {
    model: string
    entities: number
    projection: string
    /** null for the clustered (non-linear) layout */
    explainedVariance: number[] | null
    relation: string
    formula: string
    universe: number
    topK: number
    /** Graph degree summary; present once `degree.bin` is written. */
    degree?: { min: number; median: number; p99: number; max: number }
  }
  types: { name: string; count: number }[]
  /** Optional: written once the layout is clustered; `clusters.bin` indexes into it. */
  clusters?: { id: number; label: string; size: number; dominantType: string; color?: string }[]
  als: { id: string; row: number; pos: Vec3; label: string }
  profiles: DrkgProfile[]
  handWritten: { drug: string; lane: number; source: string; id: string | null; rank: number | null; distance: number | null }[]
}

export type DrkgData = { scene: DrkgScene; positions: Float32Array; types: Uint8Array; clusters: Uint8Array | null; degree: Uint32Array | null }

/** A run is a folder: `scene.json` plus the binaries written beside it. Point `src` at a live backend's run. */
export const DEFAULT_SRC = '/drkg/scene.json'

const dirOf = (src: string) => src.slice(0, src.lastIndexOf('/') + 1)

async function get(url: string) {
  const res = await fetch(url)
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${url}: ${res.status}`)
  return res
}

const runs = new Map<string, Promise<DrkgData>>()
const nameCache = new Map<string, Promise<Record<string, string>>>()

export function loadDrkg(src = DEFAULT_SRC) {
  let run = runs.get(src)
  if (run) return run
  const base = dirOf(src)
  run = Promise.all([
    get(src).then((r) => r.json() as Promise<DrkgScene>),
    get(base + 'points.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer()),
    get(base + 'types.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer()),
    get(base + 'clusters.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer(), () => null),
    get(base + 'degree.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer(), () => null),
  ]).then(([scene, p, t, c, d]) => ({
    scene,
    positions: new Float32Array(p),
    types: new Uint8Array(t),
    // Vite's dev server answers a missing file with index.html, so check the length too.
    clusters: c && c.byteLength === t.byteLength && scene.clusters ? new Uint8Array(c) : null,
    degree: d && d.byteLength === t.byteLength * 4 && scene.meta.degree ? new Uint32Array(d) : null,
  }))
  runs.set(src, run)
  run.catch(() => runs.delete(src)) // let a later mount retry
  return run
}

/** Hover labels for every entity; ~1 MB, so only fetched on first hover. */
export function loadNames(src = DEFAULT_SRC) {
  let names = nameCache.get(src)
  if (!names) {
    names = get(dirOf(src) + 'names.json').then((r) => r.json())
    nameCache.set(src, names)
    names.catch(() => nameCache.delete(src))
  }
  return names
}

export function useDrkg(src = DEFAULT_SRC) {
  const [state, setState] = useState<{ data: DrkgData | null; error: string | null }>({ data: null, error: null })
  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true
    loadDrkg(src).then(
      (data) => live && setState({ data, error: null }),
      (e: Error) => live && setState({ data: null, error: e.message }),
    )
    return () => {
      live = false
    }
  }, [src])
  return state
}

def layout_centres(C: np.ndarray, rho: np.ndarray, gap: float = 0.6, steps: int = 400) -> np.ndarray:
    """PCA-3 of the centroids (related islands sit near each other), then push apart until
    no two islands overlap."""
    Cc = C - C.mean(axis=0)
    ev, vec = np.linalg.eigh(Cc.T @ Cc)
    P3 = Cc @ vec[:, np.argsort(ev)[::-1][:3]]
    P3 *= 8.0 / np.linalg.norm(P3, axis=1).max()
    for _ in range(steps):
        moved = False
        for i in range(len(P3)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(P3)):
                d = P3[j] - P3[i]
                dist = np.linalg.norm(d) or 1e-6
                need = rho[i] + rho[j] + gap
                if dist < need:
                    push = (need - dist) / 2 * d / dist
                    P3[i] -= push
                    P3[j] += push
                    moved = True
        if not moved:
            break
    return P3


def load_triples(ent: dict[str, int], rel: dict[str, int], force: bool) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """All DRKG triples as int32 (head row, relation row, tail row). One slow parse, cached."""
    path = CACHE / "triples.npz"
    if path.exists() and not force:
        z = np.load(path)
        return z["h"], z["r"], z["t"]
    h, r, t = (np.empty(5_874_261, np.int32) for _ in range(3))
    i = 0
    with (RAW / "drkg.tsv").open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for i, line in enumerate(fh):
            a, b, c = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            h[i], r[i], t[i] = ent[a], rel[b], ent[c]
    assert i + 1 == len(h), i
    CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    np.savez(path, h=h, r=r, t=t)
    return h, r, t


def build_layout(E: np.ndarray) -> dict:
    mu = E.mean(axis=0)
    X = E - mu
    evals, evecs = np.linalg.eigh(X.T @ X / len(E))
    W50 = evecs[:, np.argsort(evals)[::-1][:PCA_DIMS]]
    Z = X @ W50
    labels, C = kmeans(Z, K_CLUSTERS)
    sizes = np.bincount(labels, minlength=K_CLUSTERS)
    rho = ISLAND * np.cbrt(sizes / sizes.mean())  # equal visual density per island
    centre = layout_centres(C, rho)
    local_W, local_s = [], []
    for k in range(K_CLUSTERS):
        res = Z[labels == k] - C[k]
        ev, vec = np.linalg.eigh(res.T @ res / len(res))
        Wk = vec[:, np.argsort(ev)[::-1][:3]]
        local_W.append(Wk)
        local_s.append(rho[k] / max(np.percentile(np.linalg.norm(res @ Wk, axis=1), 90), 1e-9))
    raw3 = np.empty((len(E), 3))
    for k in range(K_CLUSTERS):
        m = labels == k
        raw3[m] = centre[k] + (Z[m] - C[k]) @ local_W[k] * local_s[k]
    s = 10.0 / np.percentile(np.linalg.norm(raw3, axis=1), 98)
    return {"mu": mu, "W50": W50, "C": C, "rho": rho, "centre": centre, "local_W": np.stack(local_W),
            "local_s": np.asarray(local_s), "s": np.float64(s), "labels": labels.astype(np.uint8),
            "pts": (raw3 * s).astype("<f4")}


def placer(L: dict):
    """Place a non-entity vector (a query point) on its nearest island, same map as points.bin."""
    def P(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        z = (x - L["mu"]) @ L["W50"]
        k = int(np.argmin(((L["C"] - z) ** 2).sum(axis=1)))
        off = (z - L["C"][k]) @ L["local_W"][k] * L["local_s"][k]
        norm = np.linalg.norm(off)
        if norm > 1.5 * L["rho"][k]:  # an outlying query stays on the island's rim
            off *= 1.5 * L["rho"][k] / norm
        return (L["centre"][k] + off) * L["s"]
    return P


def load_labels(ent: dict[str, int]) -> tuple[dict[str, str], dict[str, list[str]]]:
    het_name: dict[str, str] = {}
    gene_symbol: dict[str, list[str]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
    with (RAW / "hetionet-v1.0-nodes.tsv").open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        next(fh)
        for line in fh:
            hid, name, kind = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            het_name[hid] = name
            if kind == "Gene":
                gene_symbol[name.upper()].append(hid)
    label: dict[str, str] = {k: v for k, v in het_name.items() if k in ent}
    kg = git_json("origin/cursor/pipeline-graph-ui:data/kg_scores.json")
    for c in (kg or {}).get("compounds", []):
        if c["drkg_id"] in ent and c.get("name") and c["drkg_id"] not in label:
            label[c["drkg_id"]] = c["name"]
    levi = git_json("origin/agentic-query-generation:backend/query-generation/snapshots/alex-gated.json")
    for cid, name in (levi or {}).get("ingredient_names", {}).items():
        if cid in ent:
            label.setdefault(cid, name)
    # Hetionet and DrugCentral cover almost no biologics or investigationals; Wikidata's
    # DrugBank-ID property (P715) does. Optional: skipped with a warning if not fetched.
    wiki = RAW / "wikidata-drugbank-names.tsv"
    if wiki.exists():
        with wiki.open(encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            next(fh)
            for line in fh:
                db, name = (x.strip().strip('"').removesuffix('"@en') for x in line.rstrip("\n").split("\t", 1))
                if f"Compound::{db}" in ent:
                    label.setdefault(f"Compound::{db}", name)
    else:
        print(f"warning: {wiki} missing; most biologic/investigational compounds stay unnamed", file=sys.stderr)
    for k, v in label.items():
        if k.startswith("Compound::"):
            label[k] = v[:1].upper() + v[1:]
    label[ALS] = "Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis"
    return label, gene_symbol


def unmapped_label(u: dict) -> str:
    """Levi's `unmapped` entries come as {target}, {proposal} or a bare {goal}."""
    if "target" in u:
        return u["target"].get("symbol", "?")
    goal = (u.get("proposal") or u).get("goal", "unmapped proposal")
    return goal if len(goal) <= 60 else goal[:57] + "…"


def levi_profiles(snapshot: Path) -> list[dict]:
    """Levi's agents -> profiles of precomputed queries (anchor, formula, ranked top_k)."""
    out = []
    for slug, title in LEVI_AGENTS.items():
        d = snapshot / "handoff" / slug
        if not (d / "trace.json").exists():
            print(f"warning: {d} has no trace.json; agent skipped", file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        trace = json.loads((d / "trace.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        ranking = json.loads((d / "ranking.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        out.append({"lane": len(out), "name": title, "agent": slug, "rankType": ranking.get("rank_type"),
                    "queries": trace.get("queries") or [], "top_k": ranking.get("top_k") or [],
                    "unresolved": [unmapped_label(u) for u in trace.get("unmapped") or []]})
    return out


def parse_formula(formula: str, E: np.ndarray, R: np.ndarray, ent: dict, rel: dict) -> np.ndarray:
    """'e[X] - r[A] + r[B]' -> e[X] - r[A] + r[B], with Levi's exact relation names."""
    m = re.match(r"e\[(.+?)\]", formula)
    q = np.asarray(E[ent[m.group(1)]], dtype=np.float64).copy()
    for sign, name in re.findall(r"([+-])\s*r\[(.+?)\]", formula[m.end():]):
        q += (1 if sign == "+" else -1) * R[rel[name]]
    return q


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    src = ap.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    src.add_argument("--profiles", type=Path, help="JSON list of {lane, name, targets}")
    src.add_argument("--from-levi", type=Path, help="Levi snapshot dir containing handoff/<agent>/")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=OUT / "scene.json")
    ap.add_argument("--relayout", action="store_true", help="rebuild layout + triple cache")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    t0 = time.time()
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    ent = load_index(RAW / "embed" / "entities.tsv")
    rel = load_index(RAW / "embed" / "relations.tsv")
    names_by_row = sorted(ent, key=ent.get)
    rel_by_row = sorted(rel, key=rel.get)
    n = len(names_by_row)
    E = np.load(RAW / "embed" / "DRKG_TransE_l2_entity.npy", mmap_mode="r")
    R = np.load(RAW / "embed" / "DRKG_TransE_l2_relation.npy").astype(np.float64)
    assert E.shape == (n, 400), E.shape
    kinds = [name.split("::", 1)[0] for name in names_by_row]

    # --- cached: triples index, layout ------------------------------------------------
    relayout = args.relayout or not (CACHE / "layout.npz").exists() or not all((OUT / f).exists() for f in LAYOUT_BINS)
    H, Rr, T = load_triples(ent, rel, force=args.relayout)
    if relayout:
        L = build_layout(np.asarray(E, dtype=np.float64))
        np.savez(CACHE / "layout.npz", **{k: v for k, v in L.items() if k not in ("labels", "pts")})
        counts = collections.Counter(kinds).most_common()
        type_index = {k: i for i, (k, _) in enumerate(counts)}
        degree = (np.bincount(H, minlength=n) + np.bincount(T, minlength=n)).astype("<u4")
        (OUT / "points.bin").write_bytes(L["pts"].tobytes())
        (OUT / "types.bin").write_bytes(np.asarray([type_index[k] for k in kinds], np.uint8).tobytes())
        (OUT / "clusters.bin").write_bytes(L["labels"].tobytes())
        (OUT / "degree.bin").write_bytes(degree.tobytes())
    else:
        L = dict(np.load(CACHE / "layout.npz"))
    pts = np.frombuffer((OUT / "points.bin").read_bytes(), "<f4").reshape(-1, 3)
    clusters_of = np.frombuffer((OUT / "clusters.bin").read_bytes(), np.uint8)
    degree = np.frombuffer((OUT / "degree.bin").read_bytes(), "<u4")
    P = placer(L)
    type_counts = collections.Counter(kinds).most_common()

    # --- names ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    label, gene_symbol = load_labels(ent)
    if relayout:  # hover labels: GO terms are long and nobody hovers them at an expo
        hover = {str(ent[k]): v for k, v in label.items()
                 if k.split("::", 1)[0] not in {"Biological Process", "Molecular Function", "Cellular Component"}}
        (OUT / "names.json").write_text(json.dumps(hover, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")), encoding="utf-8")

    # --- clusters: labelled by composition only, no invented biology -------------------
    plural = lambda t: "ATC codes" if t == "Atc" else t + ("es" if t.endswith("s") else "s")
    sizes = np.bincount(clusters_of, minlength=K_CLUSTERS)
    clusters = []
    for k in range(K_CLUSTERS):
        c = collections.Counter(kinds[i] for i in np.flatnonzero(clusters_of == k))
        top = [{"name": t, "share": round(v / sizes[k], 3)} for t, v in c.most_common(3)]
        shown = [t for t in top if t["share"] >= 0.1][:2] or top[:1]
        clusters.append({"id": k, "size": int(sizes[k]), "dominantType": top[0]["name"], "topTypes": top,
                         "label": " · ".join(f"{plural(t['name'])} {round(t['share'] * 100)}%" for t in shown)})

    # --- graph helpers over the cached triples -----------------------------------------
    is_compound = np.asarray([k == "Compound" for k in kinds])

    def compound_neighbours(row: int) -> dict[int, list[str]]:
        """compound row -> relation names, for every edge between `row` and a compound."""
        out: dict[int, list[str]] = collections.defaultdict(list)
        for side, other in ((H == row, T), (T == row, H)):
            idx = np.flatnonzero(side)
            for o, r_ in zip(other[idx], Rr[idx]):
                if is_compound[o]:
                    out[int(o)].append(rel_by_row[r_])
        return out

    def als_edge(row: int) -> str | None:
        a = ent[ALS]
        idx = np.flatnonzero(((H == row) & (T == a)) | ((H == a) & (T == row)))
        return rel_by_row[Rr[idx[0]]] if len(idx) else None

    def edges_for(row: int, nb: dict[int, list[str]], match_rows: set[int], dist_of) -> list[dict]:
        ranked = sorted(nb, key=lambda c: (c not in match_rows, names_by_row[c] not in label, dist_of(c), c))
        keep = [c for c in ranked if c in match_rows or names_by_row[c] in label][:EDGE_CAP]
        return [{"from": row, "to": c, "rel": RELATION if RELATION in nb[c] else nb[c][0]} for c in keep]

    uni_rows = np.asarray([i for i, k in enumerate(names_by_row) if UNIVERSE.match(k)])
    U = np.asarray(E[uni_rows], dtype=np.float64)
    uni_pos = {int(r_): i for i, r_ in enumerate(uni_rows)}
    name_of = lambda row: label.get(names_by_row[row], names_by_row[row].split("::", 1)[1])

    scene_profiles: list[dict] = []
    hand_out: list[dict] = []
    if args.from_levi:
        # --- Levi's agents: his anchors, his formulas, his ranks; our vectors as the check
        for p in levi_profiles(args.from_levi):
            genes, qvecs = [], []
            for q in p["queries"]:
                a = ent[q["anchor"]]
                qv = parse_formula(q["formula"], E, R, ent, rel)
                qvecs.append(qv)
                genes.append({"symbol": q.get("anchor_label") or name_of(a), "id": q["anchor"], "row": a,
                              "pos": r3(pts[a]), "query": r3(P(qv)), "formula": q["formula"],
                              "targetEdges": int(((H == a) & is_compound[T]).sum() + ((T == a) & is_compound[H]).sum()),
                              "alsEdge": als_edge(a)})
            matches = []
            for m in sorted(p["top_k"], key=lambda m: m["rank"])[:TOP_K]:
                c = ent[m["id"]]
                ours = float(np.linalg.norm(np.asarray(E[c], np.float64) - qvecs[m["query"]]))
                assert abs(ours - m["l2"]) < 1e-3, f"{p['agent']} {m['id']}: Levi l2 {m['l2']} vs ours {ours}"
                anchor = ent[p["queries"][m["query"]]["anchor"]]
                matches.append({"rank": m["rank"], "id": m["id"], "row": c, "name": name_of(c), "pos": r3(pts[c]),
                                "distance": round(m["l2"], 3), "viaGene": genes[m["query"]]["symbol"],
                                "directEdge": c in compound_neighbours(anchor)})
            match_rows = {m["row"] for m in matches}
            edges = []
            for q, g in zip(p["queries"], genes):
                if any(e["from"] == g["row"] for e in edges):
                    continue  # several queries can share one anchor
                edges += edges_for(g["row"], compound_neighbours(g["row"]), match_rows, lambda c: 0)
                for h_, r_, t_ in q.get("derivation") or []:  # multi-hop witness, e.g. gene -> GO process
                    edges.append({"from": ent[h_], "to": ent[t_], "rel": r_})
            scene_profiles.append({"lane": p["lane"], "name": p["name"], "agent": p["agent"],
                                   "rankType": p["rankType"], "genes": genes, "unresolved": p["unresolved"],
                                   "matches": matches, "edges": edges})
        projection_note = f"Levi snapshot {args.from_levi.as_posix()}"
    else:
        # --- profiles: target genes -> e[gene] - r[target] -> L2 over Compound::DB* -----
        if args.profiles:
            profiles, hand = json.loads(args.profiles.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), []
        else:
            profiles, hand = parse_pipeline()
        r_target = R[rel[RELATION]]
        profile_rank: dict[int, dict[int, tuple[int, float]]] = {}
        for p in profiles:
            genes_rows, unresolved = [], []
            for raw in p["targets"]:
                sym = re.sub(r"\s*\(.*?\)", "", raw).strip()  # "RET (GDNF)" -> RET
                if sym in ent and sym.startswith("Gene::"):
                    genes_rows.append(ent[sym])
                    continue
                hits = [h for h in gene_symbol.get(sym.upper(), []) if h in ent]
                if len(hits) == 1:
                    genes_rows.append(ent[hits[0]])
                else:
                    unresolved.append(sym)
            if not genes_rows:
                scene_profiles.append({"lane": p["lane"], "name": p["name"], "genes": [],
                                       "unresolved": unresolved, "matches": [], "edges": []})
                continue
            D = np.stack([np.linalg.norm(U - (np.asarray(E[g], np.float64) - r_target), axis=1) for g in genes_rows])
            best, via = D.min(axis=0), D.argmin(axis=0)
            order_ = np.argsort(best, kind="stable")
            profile_rank[p["lane"]] = {int(uni_rows[i]): (r_ + 1, float(best[i])) for r_, i in enumerate(order_)}
            nbs = {g: compound_neighbours(g) for g in genes_rows}
            matches = []
            for r_, i in enumerate(order_[:TOP_K]):
                c, g = int(uni_rows[i]), genes_rows[via[i]]
                matches.append({"rank": r_ + 1, "id": names_by_row[c], "row": c, "name": name_of(c),
                                "pos": r3(pts[c]), "distance": round(float(best[i]), 3),
                                "viaGene": name_of(g), "directEdge": c in nbs[g]})
            match_rows = {m["row"] for m in matches}
            edges = []
            for gi, g in enumerate(genes_rows):
                edges += edges_for(g, nbs[g], match_rows, lambda c, gi=gi: D[gi][uni_pos[c]] if c in uni_pos else 1e9)
            scene_profiles.append({
                "lane": p["lane"], "name": p["name"],
                "genes": [{"symbol": name_of(g), "id": names_by_row[g], "row": g, "pos": r3(pts[g]),
                           "query": r3(P(np.asarray(E[g], np.float64) - r_target)),
                           "targetEdges": sum(len(v) for v in nbs[g].values()), "alsEdge": als_edge(g)}
                          for g in genes_rows],
                "unresolved": unresolved, "matches": matches, "edges": edges,
            })

        # --- where the hand-written drugs land (default profiles only: lanes must match)
        by_name: dict[str, str] = {}
        by_first_word: dict[str, str] = {}  # "Somatropin recombinant" is how DRKG names somatropin
        for k, v in label.items():
            if k.startswith("Compound::"):
                by_name.setdefault(v.lower(), k)
                by_first_word.setdefault(v.lower().split(" ")[0], k)
        for drug, lane, source in hand:
            cid = by_name.get(drug.lower()) or by_first_word.get(drug.lower())
            rank_, dist = profile_rank.get(lane, {}).get(ent[cid], (None, None)) if cid else (None, None)
            hand_out.append({"drug": drug, "lane": lane, "source": source, "id": cid, "rank": rank_,
                             "distance": None if dist is None else round(dist, 3)})
        projection_note = "profiles " + (args.profiles.as_posix() if args.profiles else "pipeline.ts PROFILES")

    scene = {
        "meta": {
            "model": "DRKG pretrained TransE_l2, 400d", "entities": n,
            "projection": (f"Clustered layout: k-means (k={K_CLUSTERS}) on PCA-{PCA_DIMS} of the 400-d vectors; "
                           "islands placed by PCA-3 of the centroids, points by per-cluster local PCA-3. "
                           "Not distance-preserving."),
            "explainedVariance": None,
            "relation": "per query (see genes[].formula)" if args.from_levi else RELATION,
            "formula": ("q rebuilt from each Levi query formula; d = ‖e[c] − q‖₂ in 400-d; ranks are Levi's"
                        if args.from_levi else
                        "q = e[gene] − r[target]; d(c) = ‖e[c] − q‖₂ in 400-d; profile distance = min over its genes"),
            "source": projection_note,
            "universe": len(uni_rows), "topK": TOP_K,
            "degree": {"min": int(degree.min()), "median": int(np.median(degree)),
                       "p99": int(np.percentile(degree, 99)), "max": int(degree.max())},
        },
        "types": [{"name": k, "count": c} for k, c in type_counts],
        "clusters": clusters,
        "als": {"id": ALS, "row": ent[ALS], "pos": r3(pts[ent[ALS]]), "label": "Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis"},
        "profiles": scene_profiles,
        "handWritten": hand_out,
    }
    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.out.write_text(json.dumps(scene, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")

    # --- check (runnable, fails loudly if the maths or the wiring breaks) ---------------
    assert len(pts) == n and len(clusters_of) == n and len(degree) == n and sizes.sum() == n
    assert degree.sum() == 2 * len(H), "degree.bin is stale against the triples cache"
    for sp in scene_profiles:  # every query point lands inside the drawn scene
        for g in sp["genes"]:
            assert np.linalg.norm(g["query"]) < 15, g
    il6r = next((g for g in gene_symbol.get("IL6R", []) if g in ent), None)
    if il6r and not args.from_levi:
        nb = compound_neighbours(ent[il6r])
        known = [c for c, rels in nb.items() if RELATION in rels and c in uni_pos]
        d = np.linalg.norm(U - (np.asarray(E[ent[il6r]], np.float64) - R[rel[RELATION]]), axis=1)
        rank_of = {int(uni_rows[i]): r_ + 1 for r_, i in enumerate(np.argsort(d))}
        best_known = min(rank_of[c] for c in known)
        assert best_known <= 300, f"IL6R's own DrugBank targets rank no better than {best_known}"
        print(f"check: IL6R's DrugBank-target compounds best rank {best_known}/{len(uni_rows)} "
              f"({', '.join(name_of(c) for c in known)})")

    # --- summary ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    print(f"{'relayout' if relayout else 'cached layout'} · {projection_note} · universe {len(uni_rows)}")
    if relayout:
        for cl in clusters:
            print(f"   cluster {cl['id']:2}  {cl['size']:6}  {cl['label']}")
        for i in np.argsort(degree)[::-1][:5]:
            print(f"   hub {name_of(i)[:40]:40} {names_by_row[i]:32} {degree[i]}")
    for sp in scene_profiles:
        print(f"\n[{sp['lane']}] {sp['name']}  genes {[(g['symbol'], g['targetEdges'], g['alsEdge']) for g in sp['genes']]}"
              f"  unresolved {sp['unresolved']}  edges drawn {len(sp['edges'])}")
        for m in sp["matches"]:
            print(f"   {m['rank']}. {m['name'][:30]:30} d={m['distance']:7.3f}  via {m['viaGene'][:14]:14} direct={m['directEdge']}")
    if hand_out:
        print("\nhand-written drugs, rank within their lane's profile:")
        for h in hand_out:
            print(f"   {h['source']:10} lane {h['lane']} {h['drug']:12} {h['id'] or 'NOT IN DRKG/names':22} "
                  f"rank {h['rank']}  d={h['distance']}")
    print(f"\nwrote {args.out}  ({args.out.stat().st_size / 1024:.1f} KB)  runtime {time.time() - t0:.1f}s")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
